title: Naha in 3 Days | Kokusai-dōri, Shuri Castle, Senagajima (No Car)
subtitle: No car needed: Yui Rail links Kokusai-dōri, Shuri Castle and Senagajima
summary: Three days in Naha without ever renting a car: Makishi Public Market and Tsuboya Pottery Street, Kokusai-dōri, Shuri Castle Park and Tamaudun, Naminoue Shrine, and finally Senagajima. The notes cover getting between the airport and town, Yui Rail tickets, the current state of Shuri Castle and getting to Senagajima. Fukushū-en, Shikina-en and the Kinjō stone-paved road are held as alternates.

What this template is
A no-car template: only Yui Rail (ゆいレール), buses, taxis and walking, staying around Makishi and Kokusai-dōri and moving about central Naha and Senagajima.
For central and northern Okinawa (Churaumi, Onna, Chatan), see the separate self-drive template.
Between the airport and town (Naha Airport, OKA)

Yui Rail: Airport Station to Makishi Station is ¥320 one way, about 13 to 15 minutes (see the official site for times); Airport Station to Asahibashi Station is about 10 minutes; to Shuri Station is ¥360. Official fare table: https://www.yui-rail.co.jp/routemap/nahakuko/?t=fare
Taxi: from the airport to Asahibashi and the Naminoue Shrine area takes about 10 minutes and about ¥1,200 (Naminoue Shrine website); for fares to Kokusai-dōri, go by your ride-hailing app's estimate.
Departure day: take a taxi, about 15 minutes to the airport; you can also take Yui Rail to Airport Station.
Yui Rail tickets (checked on the official site, 2026-11-17)
Single tickets: Makishi to Shuri ¥290, Makishi to Asahibashi ¥250; airport to Shuri ¥360.
1-day pass (24 hours) adult ¥1,000, child ¥500; 2-day pass (48 hours) adult ¥1,800, child ¥900; buy at any station, counted from the time of purchase.
Contactless credit card payment: in use since 2025/3/28; according to the Ryukyu Shimpo, it charges at most ¥800 per day (follow the latest notice on the official site).

This template rides Yui Rail about 2 to 3 times a day, for less than a 1-day pass; single tickets or an IC card (OKICA, Suica) work out cheaper, and the 1-day pass's partner-facility discounts are only a few dozen yen.
Shuri Castle today (checked on the official site, 2026-11-17)

Being rebuilt since the 2019 fire: according to the official site the Main Hall (正殿) is completed in November 2026 and opens to visitors from midday on 2026/11/23 (Monday, public holiday); the morning that day and all of 11/22 are temporary closures.

Going inside the Main Hall requires an online reservation for a set date and time slot (one every 30 minutes); paid areas other than the Main Hall need no reservation (third-party summary; go by the official site).

Admission changes from 2026/11/23: the official fee page could not be retrieved, and a third-party summary gives adult ¥1,000, high-school student ¥760, elementary and junior-high student ¥370; before the change, adult ¥400 (Yui Rail website).
The free area and the Shureimon Gate area can be entered at no charge; if you cannot get a reservation for the Main Hall interior, you can still see the castle walls and the other paid areas.
For restoration progress and what can be entered in other areas, see https://oki-park.jp/shurijo/ .
Reservations and tickets
Shuri Castle Main Hall interior: reserve a date and time on the official site; peak season and the early days after opening fill up easily, so book early.
Yakiniku Ryūkyū no Ushi: reservation required.

Churasun 6: reserve on the official site https://www.churasun6.com/ ; ages 20 and over only, first-show tickets from about ¥6,500 including one drink; apart from high-fives and photos, touching the dancers is strictly forbidden.
Getting to Senagajima
From the airport: on weekends and public holidays there is a Senagajima airport shuttle bus (TK04, Tokyo Bus), adult ¥250; none on weekdays; about 10 minutes from the airport to Senagajima.
From Kokusai-dōri: the Umikaji Liner (ウミカジライナー, TK02) bound for Itoman; for detailed times and fares see https://www.umikajiterrace.com/accessguide/ , or call Tokyo Bus on 098-850-0011.
A taxi is the simplest; you can also call one from the island for the return trip.
Season

The template is based on a July summer travelogue: Naha is very hot in summer with strong UV, so outdoor stops (the Naminoue Shrine pedestrian bridge, Senagajima, the outlet) go early or late in the day, with sun protection and water; other seasons work just as well.
Many shops on Tsuboya Pottery Street close early in the afternoon, so plan to arrive around 14:00.
The Tsuboya Pottery Museum is closed 2026/9/1 to 2027/3/31; just stroll the street and skip the museum.

notes.title: Trip overview: how the 3 days run
paragraphs: In and out of Naha Airport, with both nights around Makishi and Kokusai-dōri and no car: Yui Rail, taxis and walking take you around Naha and out to Senagajima.
Day 1: ride Yui Rail to Makishi Station, lunch around the public market, Tsuboya Pottery Street in the afternoon, then {@d1-04}, an izakaya dinner and a last stop at Don Quijote.
Day 2: Yui Rail to Shuri for Shuri Castle Park and Tamaudun, lunch around Shuri Station, then {@d2-04} in the afternoon, yakiniku for dinner and the Churasun 6 gal-bar show in the evening.
Day 3: after check-out, a taxi to {@d3-01}, then pachinko, Okinawa soba, the ASHIBINAA Outlet and Blue Seal, and a taxi to the airport in the afternoon.
Where to sleep: two nights in a row around Makishi and Kokusai-dōri, a walk from the market, the main street and Makishi Station.

Getting around: Yui Rail from the airport to Makishi Station takes about 13 to 15 minutes, ¥320 one way. For Shuri you ride Yui Rail from Makishi and then walk about 15 minutes uphill to Shureimon. A taxi is the simplest way to Senagajima and on departure day, and the Umikaji Liner also runs from Kokusai-dōri; check the official sites for times and fares. The main hall of Shuri Castle needs an online reservation, and the yakiniku place and Churasun 6 need bookings too. Check the latest timetables before you go.

Who it suits: anyone who wants Naha's market, Shuri Castle, Kokusai-dōri and Senagajima without renting a car. It works solo or with a small group; summer is very hot, so outdoor sights go early or late.

events.title: Tsuboya Pottery Street (壺屋やちむん通り)

events.title: Kokusai-dōri (国際通り): a stroll past drugstores and souvenir shops

events.title: Naminoue Shrine (波上宮): with Naminoue Beach and Gokoku-ji

leg.note: Yui Rail from Shuri Station to Asahibashi Station takes about 22 minutes, then about 15 minutes on foot to the shrine; you can also go down the slope on the other side of the shrine to the beach, which is closer than taking the pedestrian bridge

events.title: Churasun 6 Okinawa (ちゅらさん6) gal-bar show

place.name: Churasun 6 Okinawa
place.address: 〒900-0032, 沖縄県那覇市, 松山1丁目5-1 2F

events.notes: Official site: first show 20:30 (doors 20:00), second show 22:30; check days off before you go; under 20 not admitted; the show lets out around 21:30, later than the 21:00 on other days

closingLeg.note: Walk back to your lodging; the Matsuyama area is rougher at night, so go with a companion and keep to the main streets

leg.note: On foot from the outlet to the other side of the street

leg.note: About 15 minutes by taxi (Blue Seal to the airport); for international flights we recommend arriving 2 hours before departure; adjust the day's timing to your actual flight; the terminal shopping street has souvenir shops, Muji and drugstores
